Interface HostUI

All Known Implementing Classes:
Mui2UI, NeiWrapperUI, ReloadHostUI, SyncedMui2UI, VanillaUI
public interface HostUI
Connects a GUI implementation to an offscreen window.

Ordinary GuiScreen subclasses already use the built-in vanilla adapter. Implement this interface when a screen needs different drawing, input, or cleanup behavior. Register its HostUIFactory for your own screen class with UIRegistry, then open the screen through OffscreenAPI. The registry creates the adapter for you. For a single open, pass the factory directly to OffscreenAPI.open(screenSupplier, adapterFactory) without registering it.

A window knows about operating-system events and render targets. This adapter knows how its particular screen draws, accepts input, and releases resources. All callbacks run on Minecraft's client thread. The hosting stack enters the adapter's scope() before ordinary screen actions and restores it afterward.

The host keeps each adapter in a hosted entry, which tracks its layout and disposal. Entries form the window's navigation stack: pushing a child retains the parent underneath; popping the child disposes its adapter and returns to the parent.

Override the small input hooks instead of replacing onInput(FrameEvent, float) unless you need custom dispatch. Default hooks do nothing, allowing a read-only screen to implement just its screen identity, drawing, and disposal.

  • Method Details

    • scope

      default Scope scope()
      Supplies the temporary Minecraft/framework state needed by this screen. A scope borrows shared state on entry and returns it on restoration. HostUI's default implementation returns a scope that changes no state.

      For example, ScreenScope temporarily sets Minecraft's current screen to the hosted GUI. Return a retained scope instance: the host calls this method separately for entry and restoration. Creating a new scope on each call would lose the saved state. The host enters and restores it around layout, updates, input, and drawing; do not enter it again inside those callbacks.

      Returns:
      non-null scope retained for entry and restoration

    • update

      default void update()
      Advances the visible screen's logic on a client tick. HostUI's default implementation does nothing.

      Ticking is independent of the window's frame-rate limit. First layout happens during rendering, so this callback can run before onResize. Initialize any state needed here before opening the window, or wait until layout has supplied the required dimensions.

    • dispose

      void dispose()
      Releases resources owned by this adapter when its hosted entry is removed. Do not dispose borrowed global Minecraft or framework resources. The hosted entry prevents duplicate disposal calls for that entry.

      Disposal does not enter this adapter's scope. Do not assume that temporary Minecraft state supplied by the scope is active during cleanup.

    • onResize

      default void onResize(int width, int height)
      Responds after Minecraft has initialized the screen at its current GUI size.

      The host calls this during first layout, when the scaled dimensions change, or after an explicit relayout request. Returning to a parent screen can call it again with the same dimensions.

      Drawing and pointer callbacks use these same GUI units. For example, a 480 by 320 GUI has its center at (240, 160), even if its framebuffer is larger. Use these dimensions for layout and hit testing without applying the display scale again.

      Parameters:
      width - scaled GUI width, not native drawable pixel width
      height - scaled GUI height, not native drawable pixel height

    • getGuiScreen

      net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiScreen getGuiScreen()

    • draw

      void draw(net.minecraft.client.Minecraft mc, int mouseX, int mouseY, float partialTicks, long now)
      Draws the screen into the host's already prepared rendering target. The host supplies the viewport, projection, and scoped Minecraft state.
      Parameters:
      mc - client instance
      mouseX - pointer X in scaled GUI coordinates
      mouseY - pointer Y in scaled GUI coordinates, measured from the top
      partialTicks - fractional client tick for smooth animation
      now - frame's wall-clock timestamp in milliseconds, from System.currentTimeMillis()

    • onInput

      default void onInput(FrameEvent event, float partialTicks)
      Delivers one mutable frame of input in a stable order: hover, button press, button release, drag, wheel, keys, then text.

      Consumed fields are cleared so wrappers such as HEI can handle an event first and prevent the underlying screen from handling it twice. Key and mouse callbacks temporarily expose the corresponding legacy LWJGL event state. Unicode text arrives separately from key transitions. The wheel callback receives only a direction, even when the accumulated delta is larger.

      Parameters:
      event - borrowed, reusable input buffer; do not retain it after dispatch
      partialTicks - fractional client tick for hover animation

      button - released Minecraft/LWJGL button index: 0 for left, 1 for right, 2 for middle

    • onMouseDrag

      default void onMouseDrag(int mouseX, int mouseY, int button, long heldMs)
      Continues a drag while the adapter's remembered button remains held.

      The default dispatcher calls this on each input pass while a drag is active, even when the pointer has not moved. Timing starts when it handles the press, so time spent waiting in the native event queue is not included.

      Parameters:
      mouseX - current pointer X in GUI units
      mouseY - current pointer Y in GUI units from the top
      button - button that started the drag
      heldMs - elapsed wall-clock milliseconds since the dispatcher handled the press

    • onMouseScroll

      default void onMouseScroll(int mouseX, int mouseY, int scroll)
      Handles the sign of this frame's accumulated wheel movement.
      Parameters:
      mouseX - pointer X in GUI units
      mouseY - pointer Y in GUI units from the top
      scroll - positive one or negative one; magnitude is normalized

    • onKeyTyped

      default void onKeyTyped(char typedChar, int keyCode)
      Handles a legacy key-down event; text composition uses onTextInput(String).

      In the default dispatcher, even a letter-key press normally carries a zero character. Use the key code for shortcuts and navigation, and handle decoded text in onTextInput rather than deriving it from that code.

      Parameters:
      typedChar - legacy character; normally zero for physical key transitions
      keyCode - LWJGL2-compatible key code

    • onKeyReleased

      default void onKeyReleased(char typedChar, int keyCode)
      Handles a legacy key-up event.
      Parameters:
      typedChar - event character, possibly zero
      keyCode - LWJGL2-compatible key code

    • onKeyPressed

      default void onKeyPressed(KeyEvent key)

      Parameters:

    • onTextInput

      default void onTextInput(String text)
      Receives decoded text independently of physical key events. A string may contain several Unicode code points; do not assume one char.
      Parameters:
      text - nonempty text accumulated for this dispatch

    • clearComponentFocus

      default void clearComponentFocus()
      Clears focused-widget state owned by this adapter. HostUI's default implementation does nothing.

      The HEI wrapper calls this when it consumes a mouse press. Implementations clear their own widget focus without changing which native desktop window has focus.
